name: pdk-polar-durable-job-enqueue
instr:
Make the background-job hand-off durable in `/app/server`. Today an API request or a worker can commit its database writes before its buffered jobs reach Redis. A Redis interruption then leaves committed customers without webhooks and ingested events without their parent links.

Jobs requested by an API request and jobs requested by another job must commit atomically with the writes that requested them; a rejected customer update must leave its previous email intact and enqueue no webhook. Customer creation and updates (`POST/PATCH /v1/customers/`) and event ingestion (`POST /v1/events/ingest`) must return their existing successful responses even if Redis is unavailable for 20 seconds. Within 30 seconds after Redis is restored, each committed customer change must result in exactly one matching `customer.created` or `customer.updated` webhook event per subscribed endpoint and one successful delivery with the existing signed payload, headers, and `webhook-id`; each ingested child event must be linked to its parent. No committed work may disappear when the API process restarts during the interruption. Follow-up `webhook_event.send` work requested by `customer.webhook` must survive the same interruption, including one occurring while that worker is active; later endpoint events must not be stranded behind it.
